title: Gas Distribution example
narrative: ON 3/1/2023 AROUND 22:30 LOCAL TIME SYSTEM MANAGEMENT WAS NOTIFIED BY EMERGENCY RESPONDERS THAT AN AUTO PARTS BUILDING THAT HAD L.P GAS SERVICE WAS ON FIRE. EMERGENCY RESPONDERS THEN CLOSED THE RISER SERVICE VALVE AND SECURED/LOCKED IT AT THAT TIME.  CAUSE OF FIRE IS UNCLEAR, ESTIMATED COST OF DAMAGES IS UNKNOWN. THE INCIDENT IS UNDER INVESTIGATION, THIS FORM IS SUBMITTED AS A PRECAUTIONARY MEASURE.

title: Gas Transmission Gathering example
narrative: DURING A ROUTINE OFFSHORE FLIGHT PATROL, A PIPELINE TECHNICIAN SPOTTED AN AREA OF BUBBLES IN THE GOM NEAR THE HIA 582 PLATFORM. THE BUBBLES WERE SUSPECTED TO BE COMING FROM THE 30" NATURAL GAS PIPELINE SEGMENT 7869. THE PIPELINE WAS ISOLATED AND MONITORED. NO SHEEN WAS OBSERVED. THE LEAK WAS REPORTED TO THE NRC AND PHMSA.    THE VISION BARGE, CONTRACTED FROM CHET MORRISSON, ARRIVED ON LOCATION. THE PIPELINE LIES AT A SEA DEPTH OF 356 FEET IN CONDITIONS OF VERY POOR VISIBILITY. SATURATION DIVERS FOUND THE PINHOLE NATURAL GAS LEAK ON THE 30" PIPELINE. THE CONCRETE AND SOMASTIC COATING ON THE PIPE WERE REMOVED AND A 30" X 24" PLIDCO CLAMP WAS BOLTED IN PLACE OVER THE LEAK. ALL UT READINGS AROUND THE CLAMP AND LEAK AREA WERE GOOD.    AN ANODE SLED WAS INSTALLED ON THE PIPE TO SUPPORT CURRENT CORROSION MITIGATION PROGRAMS. THE PIPELINE WAS TESTED UP TO 900 PSI, NORMAL OPERATING PRESSURE, AND NO LEAKS WERE OBSERVED BY THE DIVERS. THE PIPELINE WAS PLACED BACK IN SERVICE. title: Hazardous Liquid example
narrative: ON 02/02/2021 AT 6:30 PM, AN ENTERPRISE TECHNICIAN DISCOVERED A LEAK ON THE BODY BLEED OF A 4 INCH VALVE AT HOBBS STATION.  THE PIPELINE WAS SHUT DOWN AND THE VALVE WAS ISOLATED TO STOP THE LEAK.  THE PLUG WAS REMOVED AND INTERNAL CORROSION IN THE THREAD OF THE VALVE PLUG WAS OBSERVED.  THE INTERNAL CORROSION CAUSED THE VALVE PLUG TO BECOME LOOSE.     THE VALVE WAS REMOVED AND REPLACED WITH PIPING.
